s.t: A poor woodcutter lived near a forest.
s.fr: Un pauvre bûcheron vivait près d’une forêt.

s.t: He lived with his two children, Hansel and Gretel.
s.fr: Il vivait avec ses deux enfants, Hansel et Gretel.

s.t: Their mother had died when the children were young.
s.fr: Leur mère était morte quand les enfants étaient jeunes.

s.t: Soon he had a new wife, their stepmother.
s.fr: Bientôt il eut une nouvelle femme, leur belle-mère.

s.t: The stepmother did not love Hansel and Gretel.
s.fr: La belle-mère n’aimait pas Hansel et Gretel.

s.t: But that year, people had little money to buy wood.
s.fr: Mais cette année-là, les gens avaient peu d’argent pour acheter du bois.

paras.summary: A poor woodcutter lives near a forest with his two children, Hansel and Gretel, and after their mother dies when they are young, he soon has a new wife, their stepmother, who does not love them, and that year people have little money to buy wood.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel were hungry too.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel avaient faim aussi.

s.t: The stepmother did not want two hungry children.
s.fr: La belle-mère ne voulait pas deux enfants affamés.

s.t: She talked to the woodcutter.
s.fr: Elle parla au bûcheron.

s.t: "We have too little food," she said.
s.fr: « Nous avons trop peu de nourriture, » dit-elle.

s.t: "We must leave the children in the forest," said the stepmother.
s.fr: « Nous devons laisser les enfants dans la forêt, » dit la belle-mère.

s.t: He loved his children, but did not want to lose them.
s.fr: Il aimait ses enfants, mais ne voulait pas les perdre.

s.t: He agreed to the stepmother's plan.
s.fr: Il accepta le plan de la belle-mère.

paras.summary: Hansel and Gretel are hungry too, and the stepmother, not wanting two hungry children, talks to the woodcutter and says they have too little food and must leave the children in the forest, and though he loves his children and does not want to lose them, he agrees to her plan.

s.t: Soon, Hansel and Gretel were too hungry to sleep.
s.fr: Bientôt, Hansel et Gretel avaient trop faim pour dormir.

s.t: They heard the stepmother's plan.
s.fr: Ils entendirent le plan de la belle-mère.

s.t: The poor woodcutter wanted food for his hungry children.
s.fr: Le pauvre bûcheron voulait de la nourriture pour ses enfants affamés.

s.t: Gretel cried.
s.fr: Gretel pleura.

s.t: "Do not cry, Gretel," said Hansel.
s.fr: « Ne pleure pas, Gretel », dit-il Hansel.

s.t: He got up and went outside.
s.fr: Il se leva et sortit dehors.

paras.summary: Soon Hansel and Gretel are too hungry to sleep, and they hear the stepmother's plan, for the poor woodcutter wants food for his hungry children, so Gretel cries, but Hansel tells her not to cry and gets up and goes outside.

s.t: White stones shone near the house in the moonlight.
s.fr: Des pierres blanches brillaient près de la maison au clair de lune.

s.t: Hansel filled his pockets with the stones.
s.fr: Hansel remplit ses poches de pierres.

s.t: He lay near Gretel.
s.fr: Il s’allongea près de Gretel.

s.t: "Do not be afraid," he said.
s.fr: « N’aie pas peur », dit-il.

s.t: Soon the children slept.
s.fr: Bientôt les enfants s’endormirent.

paras.summary: White stones shine near the house in the moonlight, so Hansel fills his pockets with the stones, then lies near Gretel, tells her not to be afraid, and soon the children sleep.

s.t: Soon, the family left the house and walked to the forest.
s.fr: Bientôt, la famille quitta la maison et marcha vers la forêt.

s.t: The woodcutter said they would cut wood.
s.fr: Le bûcheron dit qu’ils couperaient du bois.

s.t: Hansel walked behind the family.
s.fr: Hansel marcha derrière la famille.

s.t: He took a stone from his pocket.
s.fr: Il prit une pierre dans sa poche.

s.t: He dropped the stone on the path.
s.fr: Il laissa tomber la pierre sur le chemin.

s.t: Hansel did this again and again.
s.fr: Hansel fit cela encore et encore.

paras.summary: Soon the family walks into the forest to cut wood, and Hansel, walking behind the family, takes a stone from his pocket and drops it on the path, doing this again and again.

s.t: Soon, the family came to a deep part of the forest.
s.fr: Bientôt, la famille arriva à une partie profonde de la forêt.

s.t: The woodcutter made a fire for them from wood he had cut.
s.fr: Le bûcheron fit un feu pour eux avec du bois qu’il avait coupé.

s.t: "Wait here. We must cut wood," said the woodcutter.
s.fr: « Attendez ici. Nous devons couper du bois, » dit le bûcheron.

s.t: The woodcutter did not want to leave them alone.
s.fr: Le bûcheron ne voulait pas les laisser seuls.

s.t: The stepmother and the woodcutter walked away.
s.fr: La belle-mère et le bûcheron s’éloignèrent.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel waited by the fire.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel attendirent près du feu.

s.t: The fire grew small, and night came.
s.fr: Le feu devint petit, et la nuit arriva.

s.t: The children were alone in the dark forest.
s.fr: Les enfants étaient seuls dans la forêt sombre.

paras.summary: Soon the family comes to a deep part of the forest, where the woodcutter makes a fire for the children and tells them to wait while he and the stepmother cut wood, for the poor children have little money, but though the woodcutter does not want to leave them, the stepmother and the woodcutter walk away, and as Hansel and Gretel wait by the fire, it grows small, night comes, and the children are alone in the dark forest.

s.t: Gretel cried again.
s.fr: Gretel pleura encore.

s.t: "The moon will show the way home," said Hansel.
s.fr: « La lune montrera le chemin vers la maison, » dit-il, Hansel.

s.t: The white stones shone in the moonlight.
s.fr: Les pierres blanches brillèrent dans la lumière de la lune.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel followed the stones.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel suivirent les pierres.

s.t: They walked in the night.
s.fr: Ils marchèrent dans la nuit.

s.t: Soon they saw their house.
s.fr: Bientôt ils virent leur maison.

paras.summary: Gretel cries again, but Hansel says the moon will show them the way home, and the white stones shine in the moonlight, so Hansel and Gretel follow the stones and walk in the night until soon they see their house.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel went to the house.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel allèrent à la maison.

s.t: The woodcutter came outside and saw the children.
s.fr: Le bûcheron sortit dehors et vit les enfants.

s.t: He was glad to see Hansel and Gretel.
s.fr: Il était heureux de voir Hansel et Gretel.

s.t: But the stepmother was not glad.
s.fr: Mais la belle-mère n’était pas contente.

s.t: The house still had little food.
s.fr: La maison avait encore peu de nourriture.

s.t: Soon winter came, and food grew scarce.
s.fr: Bientôt l’hiver arriva, et la nourriture devint rare.

s.t: The children grew thin and cold.
s.fr: Les enfants devinrent maigres et froids.

s.t: That winter, the stepmother wanted to leave the children again.
s.fr: Cet hiver-là, la belle-mère voulut abandonner les enfants encore.

paras.summary: Hansel and Gretel go to the house, and the woodcutter comes outside and, seeing the children, is glad, but the stepmother is not glad, and though Hansel and Gretel are glad to be home again, the house still has little food, so winter comes, food grows scarce, the children grow thin and cold, and the stepmother wants to leave the children again.

s.t: That night, Hansel heard the stepmother again.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, Hansel entendit encore la belle-mère.

s.t: "We must leave the children again," she said.
s.fr: « Nous devons abandonner les enfants encore, » dit-elle.

s.t: Hansel got up again for stones.
s.fr: Hansel se leva encore pour chercher des pierres.

s.t: But the door would not open.
s.fr: Mais la porte ne voulut pas s’ouvrir.

s.t: The stepmother had locked the door.
s.fr: La belle-mère avait fermé la porte à clé.

paras.summary: That night Hansel hears the stepmother say they must leave the children again, so he gets up for more stones, but the door will not open, for the stepmother has locked it, and Hansel cannot go outside.

s.t: He went back to Gretel.
s.fr: Il retourna vers Gretel.

s.t: "The door is locked," he said.
s.fr: « La porte est verrouillée », dit-il.

s.t: Gretel was afraid again.
s.fr: Gretel avait peur à nouveau.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel waited in the house.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel attendirent dans la maison.

s.t: The house was cold.
s.fr: La maison était froide.

s.t: "I have bread from supper," said Hansel.
s.fr: « J’ai du pain du souper », dit Hansel.

s.t: "I will drop crumbs, not stones," he said.
s.fr: « Je vais laisser des miettes, pas des pierres », dit-il.

s.t: Hansel broke the bread apart.
s.fr: Hansel brisa le pain en morceaux.

paras.summary: He goes back to Gretel and tells her the door is locked, and though she is afraid again, Hansel and Gretel wait in the cold house until Hansel says he has bread from supper and will drop crumbs instead of stones, and he breaks the bread apart.

s.t: Soon, the family walked to the forest again.
s.fr: Bientôt, la famille marcha vers la forêt à nouveau.

s.t: The children were hungry again.
s.fr: Les enfants avaient faim à nouveau.

s.t: But this time, they walked deeper in the forest.
s.fr: Mais cette fois, ils marchèrent plus loin dans la forêt.

s.t: The path grew narrow and dark.
s.fr: Le chemin devint étroit et sombre.

s.t: Hansel dropped crumbs of bread on the path.
s.fr: Hansel laissa tomber des miettes de pain sur le chemin.

s.t: Birds sat near the path and watched the crumbs fall.
s.fr: Des oiseaux s’assirent près du chemin et regardèrent les miettes tomber.

s.t: He did this again and again.
s.fr: Il fit cela encore et encore.

s.t: Gretel held Hansel's hand.
s.fr: Gretel tenait la main de Hansel.

paras.summary: Soon the family walks to the forest again, for the children are hungry again, but this time they go deeper and the path grows narrow and dark, so Hansel drops crumbs of bread on the path while birds sit nearby and watch them fall, doing this again and again, and Gretel holds Hansel's hand.

s.t: Gretel was afraid, but Hansel was not.
s.fr: Gretel avait peur, mais Hansel n’avait pas peur.

s.t: Soon, the family came to a deeper part of the forest.
s.fr: Bientôt, la famille arriva dans une partie plus profonde de la forêt.

s.t: Again, the woodcutter made a fire and said they would cut wood.
s.fr: De nouveau, le bûcheron fit un feu et dit qu’ils couperaient du bois.

s.t: The stepmother and the woodcutter left again.
s.fr: La belle-mère et le bûcheron partirent de nouveau.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel waited near the fire.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel attendirent près du feu.

s.t: Again, the fire grew small.
s.fr: De nouveau, le feu devint petit.

s.t: The children were alone in the dark forest again.
s.fr: De nouveau, les enfants étaient seuls dans la sombre forêt.

paras.summary: Gretel is afraid, but Hansel is not, and soon the family comes to a part of the forest deeper than before, where the woodcutter again makes a fire and says they will cut wood, but the stepmother and the woodcutter leave again, and as Hansel and Gretel wait near the fire, it grows small again and the children are alone in the dark forest again.

s.t: When night came, Hansel and Gretel got up.
s.fr: Quand la nuit tomba, Hansel et Gretel se levèrent.

s.t: "We can follow the crumbs home now," said Hansel.
s.fr: « Nous pouvons suivre les miettes jusqu’à la maison maintenant, » dit Hansel.

s.t: But the crumbs were gone.
s.fr: Mais les miettes avaient disparu.

s.t: Birds had eaten every crumb.
s.fr: Les oiseaux avaient mangé chaque miette.

s.t: They were lost.
s.fr: Ils étaient perdus.

paras.summary: When night comes, Hansel and Gretel get up, and Hansel says they can follow the crumbs home now, but the crumbs are gone, for birds have eaten every crumb, so Hansel and Gretel have no path to follow, and though the stones had worked, the crumbs do not, and they are lost.

s.t: The forest looked the same in every direction.
s.fr: La forêt semblait la même dans chaque direction.

s.t: Gretel cried again.
s.fr: Gretel pleura de nouveau.

s.t: Hansel was not afraid, but Gretel was.
s.fr: Hansel n’était pas effrayé, mais Gretel l’était.

s.t: "We will get home soon," he said.
s.fr: « Nous rentrerons bientôt à la maison, » dit-il.

s.t: But Hansel was not sure this time.
s.fr: Mais Hansel n’était pas sûr cette fois.

paras.summary: This time they have no stones to show them the way, and the forest looks the same in every direction, so Gretel cries again, and though Hansel is not afraid, Gretel is, but when he says they will get home soon, Hansel is not sure this time.

s.t: For three days, Hansel and Gretel walked in the forest.
s.fr: Pendant trois jours, Hansel et Gretel marchèrent dans la forêt.

s.t: They were hungry every day.
s.fr: Ils avaient faim chaque jour.

s.t: They had nothing to eat.
s.fr: Ils n’avaient rien à manger.

s.t: Gretel could not walk in the forest.
s.fr: Gretel ne pouvait pas marcher dans la forêt.

s.t: Gretel cried, for she was hungry.
s.fr: Gretel pleura, car elle avait faim.

s.t: Hansel did not want Gretel to cry.
s.fr: Hansel ne voulait pas que Gretel pleure.

paras.summary: For three days Hansel and Gretel walk in the forest, hungry every day with nothing to eat, until Gretel can not walk in the forest and cries from hunger, though Hansel does not want her to cry.

s.t: Then a white bird came to them.
s.fr: Alors, un oiseau blanc vint vers eux.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel followed the small bird.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel suivirent le petit oiseau.

s.t: The bird flew from tree to tree.
s.fr: L’oiseau vola d’arbre en arbre.

s.t: Soon, the bird led them to a small clearing.
s.fr: Bientôt, l’oiseau les conduisit à une petite clairière.

s.t: Ahead stood a strange house.
s.fr: Devant eux se dressait une maison étrange.

paras.summary: Then a white bird comes to them, and Hansel and Gretel follow it as it flies from tree to tree, until soon it leads them to a small clearing, where ahead stands a strange house.

s.t: The old house was made of bread and sugar.
s.fr: La vieille maison était faite de pain et de sucre.

s.t: The forest was dark near the strange house.
s.fr: La forêt était sombre près de l’étrange maison.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel ate the bread and sugar.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel mangèrent le pain et le sucre.

s.t: Then an old woman came from the house.
s.fr: Puis une vieille femme vint de la maison.

s.t: Hansel held Gretel's cold hand.
s.fr: Hansel tint la main froide de Gretel.

paras.summary: The strange house is made of bread and sugar in the dark forest, and Hansel and Gretel, hungry and afraid, eat the bread and sugar, so an old woman comes from the house, and Hansel holds Gretel's hand.

s.t: "Who eats my house?" said the old woman.
s.fr: « Qui mange ma maison ? » dit la vieille femme.

s.t: The old woman could not see well.
s.fr: La vieille femme ne pouvait pas bien voir.

s.t: She touched Hansel and Gretel with her cold hands.
s.fr: Elle toucha Hansel et Gretel avec ses mains froides.

s.t: "You poor children," said the old woman.
s.fr: « Vous pauvres enfants, » dit la vieille femme.

s.t: "Come inside, and I will feed you," she said.
s.fr: « Entrez, et je vous nourrirai, » dit-elle.

s.t: The poor children went inside with her.
s.fr: Les pauvres enfants entrèrent avec elle.

s.t: The old woman had a plan.
s.fr: La vieille femme avait un plan.

paras.summary: "Who eats my house?" asks the old woman, who cannot see well, so she touches Hansel and Gretel with her cold hands and, calling them poor children, invites them inside to feed them; glad for the food, the children go inside with her, no longer feeling lost, though the old woman has a plan of her own.

s.t: The old witch lived alone in the little house near the forest.
s.fr: La vieille sorcière vivait seule dans la petite maison près de la forêt.

s.t: The old witch grabbed Hansel.
s.fr: La vieille sorcière attrapa Hansel.

s.t: She put him in a cage in the house.
s.fr: Elle le mit dans une cage dans la maison.

s.t: The old witch locked the cage.
s.fr: La vieille sorcière ferma la cage à clé.

s.t: "You will grow fat here," said the witch.
s.fr: « Tu deviendras gros ici, » dit la sorcière.

s.t: "Then I will eat you," she said.
s.fr: « Ensuite je te mangerai, » dit-elle.

paras.summary: The witch, who lives alone in the little house near the forest, grabs Hansel and puts him in a cage, which she locks so he cannot get out, and she tells him he will grow fat and then she will eat him.

s.t: Gretel wanted to leave the house again, but she could not.
s.fr: Gretel voulait quitter la maison encore, mais elle ne pouvait pas.

s.t: "You must cook and clean for me," said the witch.
s.fr: « Tu dois cuisiner et nettoyer pour moi, » dit la sorcière.

s.t: Every day, Gretel did what the old witch said.
s.fr: Chaque jour, Gretel faisait ce que la vieille sorcière disait.

s.t: Gretel cooked and carried water for the witch.
s.fr: Gretel cuisinait et portait de l’eau pour la sorcière.

s.t: Every day, the witch fed Hansel a lot of food again.
s.fr: Chaque jour, la sorcière donnait à Hansel beaucoup de nourriture encore.

paras.summary: Gretel is afraid for Hansel and wants to leave, but she cannot, and the witch tells her she must cook and clean, so Gretel does what the witch says and cooks food for her, while every day the witch feeds Hansel a lot of food and every night Hansel cannot sleep, for the witch wants him to grow fat.

s.t: Hansel stayed in the cage for many days.
s.fr: Hansel resta dans la cage pendant beaucoup de jours.

s.t: The little cage was cold.
s.fr: La petite cage était froide.

s.t: Every day, the witch checked Hansel's finger.
s.fr: Chaque jour, la sorcière vérifiait le doigt de Hansel.

s.t: She wanted to know if he was fat.
s.fr: Elle voulait savoir s’il était gros.

s.t: But the witch could not see well.
s.fr: Mais la sorcière ne pouvait pas voir bien.

s.t: She touched his finger to check instead.
s.fr: Elle touchait son doigt pour vérifier à la place.

paras.summary: Hansel stays in the cold cage for many days, and every day the witch checks his finger to see if he is fat, but she cannot see well, so she touches his finger to check.

s.t: Gretel was afraid every day and cooked food for the witch.
s.fr: Gretel avait peur chaque jour et cuisinait de la nourriture pour la sorcière.

s.t: The witch went away every day.
s.fr: La sorcière partait chaque jour.

paras.summary: Gretel is afraid every day and cooks food for the witch, while the witch goes away every day.

s.t: Hansel had an old bone in the cage.
s.fr: Hansel avait un vieux os dans la cage.

s.t: He held out the bone, not his finger.
s.fr: Il tendit l’os, pas son doigt.

s.t: The witch touched the thin bone.
s.fr: La sorcière toucha le mince os.

s.t: "You are still too thin," said the witch.
s.fr: « Tu es encore trop maigre, » dit la sorcière.

s.t: The witch put Hansel back in the cage.
s.fr: La sorcière remit Hansel dans la cage.

s.t: She checked him again and again.
s.fr: Elle le vérifia encore et encore.

paras.summary: Hansel had an old bone in the cage, and he holds out the bone, not his finger, so the witch touches the thin bone, telling him he is still too thin, and she puts him back in the cage and checks him again and again, never knowing of the bone.

s.t: Hansel was still in the cage, but the witch would not wait.
s.fr: Hansel était encore dans la cage, mais la sorcière ne voulait plus attendre.

s.t: "I will cook Hansel," said the witch.
s.fr: « Je vais cuisiner Hansel, » dit la sorcière.

s.t: The witch made the oven hot.
s.fr: La sorcière rendit le four chaud.

s.t: "Gretel, look in the oven," said the witch.
s.fr: « Gretel, regarde dans le four, » dit la sorcière.

s.t: Gretel did not want to lose Hansel.
s.fr: Gretel ne voulait pas perdre Hansel.

s.t: Gretel did not know how to look in the oven.
s.fr: Gretel ne savait pas comment regarder dans le four.

s.t: "Show me how," said Gretel.
s.fr: « Montre-moi comment, » dit-elle.

s.t: The witch put her head in the oven.
s.fr: La sorcière mit sa tête dans le four.

paras.summary: Hansel is still in the cage, but the witch will not wait any longer and says she will cook him, making the oven hot, and she tells Gretel to look inside, but Gretel, not wanting to lose Hansel, does not know how and asks the witch to show her, so the witch puts her own head in the oven.

s.t: Though afraid, Gretel loved Hansel and did what she must.
s.fr: Bien que effrayée, Gretel aimait Hansel et fit ce qu’elle devait.

s.t: Gretel pushed the witch in, and she could not get out.
s.fr: Gretel poussa la sorcière dedans, et elle ne pouvait pas sortir.

s.t: Gretel shut the oven door.
s.fr: Gretel ferma la porte du four.

s.t: The old witch died alone in the hot oven.
s.fr: La vieille sorcière mourut seule dans le four chaud.

s.t: Hansel, still thin and afraid, heard the witch cry out.
s.fr: Hansel, encore maigre et effrayé, entendit la sorcière crier.

s.t: Gretel opened the cage, and Hansel came out to her.
s.fr: Gretel ouvrit la cage, et Hansel sortit vers elle.

paras.summary: Gretel, afraid but loving Hansel, pushes the witch in, and she cannot get out; Gretel shuts the oven door, and the old witch dies alone in the hot oven while Hansel, still thin and afraid, hears her cry out; her plan has not worked, and Gretel opens the cage so Hansel comes out to her.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel looked around the witch's dark house.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel regardèrent autour de la sombre maison de la sorcière.

s.t: The house had gold.
s.fr: La maison avait de l’or.

s.t: Jewels and pearls were in the house too.
s.fr: Des bijoux et des perles étaient dans la maison aussi.

s.t: Hansel filled his pockets with gold.
s.fr: Hansel remplit ses poches d’or.

s.t: Gretel filled her pockets with jewels and pearls.
s.fr: Gretel remplit ses poches de bijoux et de perles.

paras.summary: Hansel and Gretel look around the witch's dark house and find it has gold, jewels, and pearls that shine, so Hansel fills his pockets with gold and Gretel fills hers with jewels and pearls.

s.t: "We are rich," said Hansel.
s.fr: « Nous sommes riches, » dit Hansel.

s.t: "This gold will feed our family," he said.
s.fr: « Cet or nourrira notre famille, » dit-il.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel wanted to go home to see the woodcutter again.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel voulaient rentrer chez eux pour revoir le bûcheron.

s.t: Gretel held Hansel's hand and was glad to leave the dark house.
s.fr: Gretel tint la main de Hansel et était contente de quitter la maison sombre.

s.t: They left the witch's house and walked to the forest.
s.fr: Ils quittèrent la maison de la sorcière et marchèrent vers la forêt.

paras.summary: They are rich and glad now, and Hansel says the gold will feed their family, so they are not poor now, for the witch will never come back, and Hansel and Gretel, wanting to go home to see the woodcutter again, hold hands and are glad to leave the dark house and walk to the forest.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel walked to a wide water.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel marchèrent jusqu’à une large étendue d’eau.

s.t: They could not cross the water.
s.fr: Ils ne pouvaient pas traverser l’eau.

s.t: A white duck came to them.
s.fr: Un canard blanc vint vers eux.

s.t: "Will you carry us across the water?" said Hansel.
s.fr: « Voulez-vous nous porter de l’autre côté de l’eau ? » dit Hansel.

s.t: The duck carried Hansel across, and then Gretel too.
s.fr: Le canard porta Hansel de l’autre côté, puis Gretel aussi.

s.t: They thanked the white duck, and the duck flew away.
s.fr: Ils remercièrent le canard blanc, et le canard s’envola.

s.t: The water was cold and wide.
s.fr: L’eau était froide et large.

paras.summary: Hansel and Gretel walk to a wide water they cannot cross, and a white duck comes to them, so Hansel asks it to carry them across, and it carries Hansel and then Gretel; now across the cold, wide water, they thank the duck, which flies away.

s.t: They walked in the dark forest again.
s.fr: Ils marchèrent de nouveau dans la sombre forêt.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel followed the path home.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel suivirent le chemin vers la maison.

s.t: They walked for three days.
s.fr: Ils marchèrent pendant trois jours.

s.t: The forest was cold in the night.
s.fr: La forêt était froide la nuit.

s.t: They still had gold in their pockets.
s.fr: Ils avaient encore de l’or dans leurs poches.

s.t: Soon they saw their old house.
s.fr: Bientôt ils virent leur vieille maison.

paras.summary: They walk in the dark forest again, following the path home for three days through the cold nights, and though they still have gold in their pockets to feed their family, soon they see their old house.

s.t: The woodcutter was alone and sad every day.
s.fr: Le bûcheron était seul et triste chaque jour.

s.t: The stepmother was gone.
s.fr: La belle-mère était partie.

s.t: Hansel and Gretel went to him.
s.fr: Hansel et Gretel allèrent vers lui.

s.t: "You are home!" said the woodcutter.
s.fr: « Tu es à la maison ! » dit le bûcheron.

s.t: He held Hansel and Gretel again.
s.fr: Il serra Hansel et Gretel de nouveau.

s.t: The woodcutter cried from joy.
s.fr: Le bûcheron pleura de joie.

s.t: Hansel gave him the gold and jewels.
s.fr: Hansel lui donna l’or et les joyaux.

paras.summary: Hansel and Gretel come to their house, where the woodcutter has been alone and sad every day since the stepmother is gone, and when the children go to him, he says they are home and holds them again, crying from joy, and Hansel gives him the gold and jewels.

s.t: The gold shone in the woodcutter's hands.
s.fr: L’or brillait dans les mains du bûcheron.

s.t: "This gold will feed our family," said Hansel.
s.fr: « Cette or nourrira notre famille », dit Hansel.

s.t: The family was not poor now, and they were never hungry again.
s.fr: La famille n’était plus pauvre, et ils n’avaient plus jamais faim.

paras.summary: The gold shines in the woodcutter's hands, and Hansel says it will feed their family, so the family is not poor now and never hungry again, glad together forever.
